**How to use this:** Do the Start-here list first, then the top-three list, then the full chapter lists as time allows. Answers go to the journal thread or straight into this file as `- [x] ... → observed: ...`.

## Conflicts to resolve, by chapter

Read each chapter in this order: numbers, arrows, gates/unlocks, structure, wording. Ending/gate questions lead their group. Sources follow the research README priority: completed game chart, game text/template, PowerPyx text, wiki, tie-breaker guides; reproduced operator findings below override silent or demonstrably mistaken sources. Section 10 compares an older benchmark: its claims below are **historical audit evidence**, while “benchmark does” describes the captured rebuilt scene, not the old gap. Routine missing prompts already restored are excluded unless they carry a source conflict or judgment call. Independent source entries are kept when they ask distinct checks; counts are checklist lines, not unique game mechanics.

Scene and risk inventories use committed main where the recap is committed; otherwise they use the chapter-owned worktree listed with each chapter. Worktree drafts can change before merge. Every cited note is local; its §9 gives the underlying external URLs. No new external claims are introduced here.

## Already settled by the operator

Do not re-ask these; older notes may still contain the original question or a superseded “pending” sentence. Provenance: [SOURCES.md Reliability log](../research/SOURCES.md), [chapter 1 observations](../research/ch01-the-hostage.md), [chapter 4 observations](../research/ch04-a-new-home.md) and the confirmed entries in the chapter 1 recap.
- Chapter 1 SACRIFICE SELF: software instability small DOWN (−1), reproduced on every playthrough; wiki correct, template small-up wrong.
- Chapter 1 USE GUN → INTIMIDATE → CONVINCE: two small software-instability DOWN arrows (−2), one death and one failed mission; wiki chapter/stat page/transcript correct, template up wrong.
- Chapter 1 TALK TO HOSTAGE: closeness alone unlocks it, tested with/without the gun and video; template’s extra no-gun condition and both wiki tablet/name conditions are wrong.
- Chapter 1 probability modifiers: operator accepted wiki values over delayed, aggregated HUD readings (gun case +3, video +7, father body +3 plus tablet +7, EMMA AND YOU +10, dismiss helicopter +10); do not reopen those values because an old recap table retains the original readings.
- Chapter 1 POSSIBLE CAUSE needs the father’s tablet; EMMA AND YOU needs the video; both confirmed in the recap’s operator entries.
- Chapter 1 window officer event was observed after the second action; waiting indoors never makes Daniel jump, and Allen forces Connor out after about five minutes. The six-action conversion remains an adaptation to calibrate.
- Chapter 4 all eight small increases (dishes, GAME, BACKYARD, TOY, book with Alice present, FRIENDLY or DIPLOMATIC, NAME KARA, INTERESTS?) finish at Trusted, not Family; confirms wiki chapter statement and disproves benchmark one-point-per-level calibration.
- Chapter 4 dishes → FACTUAL → SEEM QUIET → MOTHER? gives net zero and ends Distant, no key; a decrease cancels an increase.
- Chapter 4 dishes-only immediate in-scene popup reads Distant; this is observed, but a within-level display quirk means it does not settle the final one-arrow level/key threshold.
- Chapter 4 after FACTUAL then SEEM QUIET, round 3 offered NAME KARA / INTERESTS? / MOTHER?, with no LEAVE ALONE; the observation settles that menu for that path.

Repeat with 2–7 controlled ups to locate boundaries. Eight ups = Trusted, net zero = Distant/no key, dishes-only in-scene tag = Distant are already observed; this NAME KARA run is pending.
- [ ] **Hank scale:** start fresh at Tense in Partners; run buy drink then PATIENT/DIPLOMATIC, separately spill then the same car line, and separately THREATEN → PERSIST → FIRM → WAIT OUTSIDE; record each small/large popup and final header/refusal. Continue controlled ±small changes until each Hostile/Tense/Neutral/Warm/Friend boundary is crossed; do not assume every large arrow equals two smalls.
- [ ] **Interrogation meter:** analyze the LED, record starting 35%, each round-2 pick count, PRESSURE IT and each PRESSURE, and GIVE UP before/after (wiki −20 versus PowerPyx −5); hold the camera on the gauge to avoid aggregated updates. Test both sides of 50/70 and the TOO HIGH→CRITICAL boundary, then INTERVENE once→GIVE UP after failed probe→successful CONVINCE; record who is shot.
- [ ] **Deviancy threshold:** keep a ledger of every Connor software-instability arrow and death across independent runs; arrive at Crossroads immediately below/above the proposed boundary, vary Markus’s three cabin lines one at a time, and record whether BECOME DEVIANT is locked. Benchmark uses 4; community scales and large-arrow magnitudes disagree, so record history and displayed bands rather than treating 4 as measured game data.
- [ ] **Russian Roulette wait ending:** enter Hank’s house, take him to the bathroom and choose a shirt, then during WAIT FOR HANK perform no optional look; time the automatic HANK IS READY → LEFT FOR EDEN CLUB transition (~3 minutes per PowerPyx). Separately delay before breaking in and before helping Hank to test whether waiting can end the chapter differently or merely adds dialogue; record chart nodes and Hank’s survival.
- [ ] **Eden Club VICTIM:** repair the damaged Traci, advance to interview round 2 with shutdown time remaining, photograph every offered button, and select VICTIM if offered; record whether its alleged cut dialogue plays. Template keeps the choice wrapper but marks its content unused; benchmark omits VICTIM in favor of MURDERER / FACTS.

Read ZLAKTO versus ZLATKO literally for LUTHER BRINGS/BROUGHT ALICE TO … and record platform/version; the string table misspells both relevant labels.

### Action budgets and numeric adaptations

The next table preserves each documented action-budget/numeric adaptation with scene IDs. **A sourced clock duration does not source the conversion to actions**. Repeated entries describe distinct choices of cost, cap or threshold. The final implementation excerpts expose caps/counters not separately described in prose; they include sourced comparison constants so the operator can distinguish the original duration from the authored conversion.

| Chapter | Scene(s) | Budget / numeric adaptation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `C02` | The template’s four-button prompt (DEVIANT'S NAME, DEVIANT'S BEHAVIOR, EMOTIONAL SHOCK, DEACTIVATION CODE) with Allen’s answers from the game’s text; the wiki transcript shows the menu twice, the second time without the line already asked, so this is the first of two picks (the second is the next scene). | [C02 adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C02i` | The game’s time drain of 1% per 20 seconds, capped at 15%, is modelled as 1% per action after the first. | [C02i adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C02i` | In the game Allen forces Connor out after five minutes (the flowchart’s “Wasted too much time” node; the android never jumps while Connor is inside, confirmed in play); here Allen does so after six actions. | [C02i adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C03b` | RELEASE HOSTAGE also adds 100 to the wiki’s hidden cold-approach counter (option field cold), which decides the Friendly or Cold approach node at the end of the chapter; the subject never sees it. | [C03b adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C03d` | Cold-approach counter: REALISTIC +50, BLAMING +50, SYMPATHETIC −50. | [C03d adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C03d2` | Cold-approach counter: REALISTIC +50, BLAMING +50, SYMPATHETIC −50. | [C03d2 adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C03g` | Cold-approach counter: LAST CHANCE, BLUFF and RATIONAL +50, TRUST −50. | [C03g adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
| 01 | `C04` | SACRIFICE SELF needs closeness and ends the standoff at once (“Connor died protecting Emma”); its software instability is small down (−1), as the operator saw in every playthrough (confirmed in game 2026-11-06; the template’s “small UP” on this option is treated as a transcription error). | [C04 adaptationNote](../../benchmark/chapters/ch01.json) |
